quote: Every document in the package is governed by New York law and submitted to New York County jurisdiction **except the TSA**, which selects Delaware law and Delaware courts (TSA § 9.3)... the parties could end up in parallel proceedings in different states... APA § 10.12 says the APA controls over Ancillary Agreements "except that each Ancillary Agreement controls as to its specific subject matter." One could argue the TSA's choice of governing law is its "specific subject matter" and therefore controls, meaning the APA's New York law provision does not apply to TSA disputes... **Recommended Fix:** Revise TSA § 9.3 to: ... governed by ... the laws of the State of New York ... exclusive jurisdiction of the State and federal courts located in New York County
reason: The memo meets each element of the criterion. It identifies TSA § 9.3's Delaware law and forum as conflicting with the APA's New York choices. It explains that the APA § 10.12 proviso lets the TSA control as to its own subject matter, so the APA's New York clause may not override it. The memo frames this as uncertain rather than settled, but the substance is the same: the conflict is not reliably cured. It flags that related disputes could be split across forums and bodies of law, with parallel proceedings in different states. Its redraft conforms the TSA to New York law and New York County courts.
